summary.title: Friendship strained after missing best friend's wedding duties
summary.what_happened: I was supposed to be my best friend's best man at his wedding. Three days before, my boss asked me to cover a client trip, and I said yes. I told him by text, and he had to find another best man at the last minute. Afterwards I sent a gift and said sorry once by text. He has been cold to me since the wedding, and it has been four months. The client was a big one and my promotion is coming up.
summary.my_feelings: I think he may be overreacting. I feel the coldness has gone on for a long time, and I am concerned about our friendship.
summary.my_needs: I need my career pressures to be understood, and I need the friendship to feel normal again.
summary.desired_outcome: I want things to go back to normal with my friend.

consult.text: It sounds like you miss your friend, and four months of coldness is a long time to carry. You also had real pressure at work, and a promotion matters. Here is how he may see it. Being best man is a big role, and he asked you because you are close. Three days before his wedding, he heard by text that you would not be there, and he had to scramble to find someone else. For him, it may feel less like a work problem and more like being told that something else mattered more on a day he cannot repeat. One thing that may have made this harder is how it was handled. A text, and a single apology by text, can feel small next to what he lost. I think he has a fair reason to be hurt, even if you had real constraints too. We do not know what he actually feels, or whether something else is behind the distance. You could ask him for a call or a meeting in person, apologise directly for the short notice and the way you told him, and ask how it felt for him. Then listen without explaining your reasons first.
I already apologised. What more does he want, me to quit my job?

No, I do not think he wants you to quit your job. That sounds like a painful thought, and I can tell you feel stuck. Your career matters, and choosing work in a tough moment does not make you a bad friend. The question is probably not the job, though. It may be how much the apology reached him. A short text and a gift can feel like a way to close the topic, not a way to meet him. He may be waiting for you to understand what the day meant to him. I cannot know that for sure. So I would not guess. Ask him. You could say that you know you let him down, that you want to hear how it was for him, and that you are not there to defend yourself. Offer to meet in person. Let him talk first. Then say what you would do differently if something like this came up again.

share_draft: Hi. I have been thinking about your wedding and about how things have felt between us since. Three days before, I said yes to a work trip and then let you know by text that I could not be your best man. I can see that left you without much time and probably hurt. I said sorry by text, but I do not think that was enough, and I would like to do better. I miss you, and I would like things to feel normal again. I also have my own side, and my work was under real pressure then, but first I would like to hear how it was for you. Would you be open to meeting or talking in person?
